question: Based on Apparent Thermal Inertia (ATI) calculated from daytime and nighttime brightness temperature and surface albedo over the urban area of Beijing, China from June 1 to September 30, 2019, list the input TIFF files, compute ATI for each pixel, investigate the monthly trend of ATI, and identify the month with the largest decrease in ATI.
final_answer_preview: The calculation of Apparent Thermal Inertia (ATI) requires surface albedo data, which is not provided in the listed files. The available files only include brightness temperature (BT) data for daytime and nighttime observations. Without albedo data, the ATI formula $ \text{ATI} = \frac{T_{\text{day}} - T_{\text{night}}}{\text{albedo}} $ cannot be computed. Please provide the albedo data files to proceed with the analysis.
